item.title: New bound on the Hausdorff dimension of Kakeya sets in $\mathbb{R}^4$
item.description: arXiv:2610.12480v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We obtain a slight improvement to the trilinear bound of Guth-Zahl by application of Wang-Zahl's resolution of 3-D Kakeya to tubes inside a thickened neighborhood of a variety. This is combined with the planebrush argument of Katz and Zahl to obtain the new bound of 3.073.
item.dc:creator: Mukul Rai Choudhuri

item.title: A higher-dimensional Schr\"odinger maximal estimate along families of bi-Lipschitz curves
item.description: arXiv:2610.12565v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\Theta\subset\mathbb{R}^n$, $n\geq 1$ be compact with upper Minkowski dimension $\beta$, and let $\gamma(x,t,\theta)$ be a family of curves which is bi-Lipschitz in the first variable and Lipschitz in the last two. We prove the maximal estimate $$\left\|\sup_{(\tau,\theta)\in[0,1)\times\Theta}\left|e^{i\tau\Delta}f(\gamma(\,\cdot\,,\tau,\theta))\right|\right\|_{L^2(B^n_1)}\lesssim_s\|f\|_{H^s(\mathbb{R}^n)},$$ for every $s>\tfrac{n(\beta+1)}{2(n+1)}$, in the range $0\le\beta\le n-1$. In the range $n-1<\beta\leq n$ we prove the threshold $s>\min\big\lbrace\frac\beta 2 + \frac 1{2(n+1)},\frac n2\big\rbrace$. The proof relies on a fractal $L^2$ estimate of Du--Zhang. We also use the temporal localization of Lee, the locally constant property, and a counting argument allowed by the Lipschitz properties of the curve.
item.dc:creator: Javier Minguill\'on

item.title: The square function estimate for the cone in four dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2610.12681v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We obtain the $L^3$ reverse square function estimate for the light cone in four dimensions from the critical local-smoothing and round-cone propagation statements in the September 2026 OpenAI manuscript. We state these inputs, together with the plate maximal theorem of Di Plinio and Parissis, in a preliminaries section. The proof passes from geometric concentration of packet coefficients to regularity of the analyzed wave, and then from free waves to arbitrary functions supported near the cone. As a consequence, we obtain the corresponding $L^3$ estimate for the sphere and elliptic paraboloids in three dimensions.
item.dc:creator: Faruk Temur

item.title: Limit cycles of slow-fast quintic Lienard systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.13080v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For every fixed real quintic polynomial $F$, we prove that the slow--fast Li\'enard system $\dot{x}=y-F(x),\quad \dot{y}=-\varepsilon x$ admits at most two limit cycles whenever $0<\varepsilon<\varepsilon_0(F)$ for a suitable $\varepsilon_0(F)>0$. Using scalar comparison near the equilibrium and a logarithmic fold-passage correction, we exclude \rev{canard singular limits}. Every sequence of limit cycles with $\varepsilon\to0^+$ has a subsequence converging in the Hausdorff metric to a common slow--fast path, whose regular slow arcs are either all normally attracting or all normally repelling. We also establish uniform Floquet separation for fixed $F$. The global counting argument uses shared regular arcs, nesting, and stability alternation. These results give a global small-parameter bound and describe the singular-limit structure, complementing the local cyclicity analysis of Li and Lu(J. Differential Equations, 2014).
item.dc:creator: Hebai Chen, Leshan Chen, Yu Xiao

item.title: Sharp power-weight estimates for the fractional spherical maximal operator
item.description: arXiv:2610.13326v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For $0\leq\alpha<n$, let $A_{*}^{\alpha}$ denote the fractional spherical maximal operator. In this paper we characterise the range of $\beta$ for which the $L^p-L^q$ power-weight estimate \[\left\|A_{*}^{\alpha} f\right\|_{L^q(|x|^{q\beta})} \leq C \left\|f\right\|_{L^p(|x|^{p\beta})}\] holds. In the diagonal case $p=q$, our work gives an affirmative answer to a conjecture of Lee. We prove analogous results for the lacunary fractional spherical maximal operator.
item.dc:creator: Riju Basak, Surjeet Singh Choudhary, Chun-Yen Shen, Daniel Spector

item.title: Hsiang cubics as spherical Chebyshev polynomials: equioscillation and idempotent quadrature
item.description: arXiv:2610.13532v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A Hsiang cubic is a cubic form on $\mathbb{R}^{n}$ whose zero set is a minimal cone; equivalently, it is the cubic form of a commutative nonassociative metrized algebra satisfying a single identity of degree four. We show that the intrinsic geometry of such an algebra, encoded in its idempotents and their Peirce decompositions, is the geometry of a Chebyshev-type extremal problem on the sphere. A Hsiang cubic equioscillates on $S^{n-1}$: its maximum set is the set of normalized idempotents, and on suitable great circles through an idempotent it restricts to the Chebyshev polynomial $T_3$. For the spherical analogue of the problem of least deviation, the minimization of $\|p\|_\infty^2/\|p\|_2^2$ over harmonic cubics, a sharp lower bound based on Kellogg's inequality shows that Cartan's isoparametric cubics are the global minimizers in dimensions $5$, $8$, $14$ and $26$. In general, we compute the ratio of every Hsiang cubic in terms of the Killing form and characterize stationarity by a Kolmogorov criterion: it amounts to a positive measure on the idempotent variety. Such measures are given explicitly in several cases which together cover every Hsiang cubic known to exist; in particular, all of them are stationary. These measures give quadrature identities on the idempotent variety whose moments are invariants of the algebra; they are spherical designs exactly in the Einstein (Killing metrized) case, i.e.\ when the Killing form is proportional to the inner product. Distinguished low-dimensional Hsiang cubics are strict local minimizers, whereas a polar Hsiang cubic is a stationary non-minimizer.
item.dc:creator: Vladimir G. Tkachev

item.title: Spread-out Furstenberg sets I: the sticky case
item.description: arXiv:2610.13677v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce spread-out measures, a notion of local non-concentration near pencils for measures on Grassmannians. We establish an optimal $\delta$-discretized dual Furstenberg estimate for ``sticky spread-out'' shadings. A simple-to-state corollary is the following. Assume that $\nu$ is an Ahlfors $s$-regular measure on $\mathbb{G}(2,1)$ with $s > 0$. Let $E \subset \mathbb{R}^{2}$ be a Borel set with equal Hausdorff and packing dimension. Then, $\dim_{\mathrm{H}} \Pi_{V}(E) = \min\{\dim_{\mathrm{H}} E,1\} \quad \text{for $\nu$-a.e. } V \in S^1$. The general $\delta$-discretized estimate for ``sticky spread out'' configurations here is the starting point for a more general theorem in the companion paper of Cohen, Shmerkin, Wang and Zakharov, where the ``stickiness'' hypothesis is removed. For instance, the assumption of equal Hausdorff and packing dimension in the result stated above will be dispensed with in the companion paper.
item.dc:creator: Tuomas Orponen, Pablo Shmerkin

item.title: Spread-out Furstenberg sets II: general configurations and fractal restricted projections
item.description: arXiv:2610.13682v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove optimal dual Furstenberg estimates for Frostman and Katz--Tao configurations for which the shadings are not locally concentrated near pencils. The starting point is the sticky estimate of Orponen and Shmerkin in a companion paper. We deduce restricted projection theorems in the plane and in higher dimensions. In particular, Ahlfors-regular measures on the circle satisfy a Marstrand-type projection theorem. Applications include restricted projections to surfaces in the $\mathbb{G}(4,2)$ Grassmannian, pinned distances, discretized sum-product, and a new proof of the dimension formula for planar self-affine sets.
item.dc:creator: Alex Cohen, Pablo Shmerkin, Hong Wang, Dmitrii Zakharov

item.title: The second type of power mean bounds for the hypergeometric mean
item.description: arXiv:2610.13699v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, by using signs rule for a class of special power series and for the Laplace integrals, we find the best power mean bounds for the hypergeometric function (sharp at the right endpoint). Our results contain many known conclusions.
item.dc:creator: Zhen-Hang Yang, Jing-Feng Tian

item.title: Characterizing higher-dimensional H\"older domains via spherical geometric functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.13866v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we characterize the regularity of a domain in terms of the behavior of a certain spherical function. More precisely, given two domains we show that a certain spherical spectral function (first defined in \cite{FTV23}, see also \cite{AKN21}) has H\"older decay if and only if the domains are complementary and separated by a $C^{1,\beta}$-manifold. This extends the analysis in \cite{Ca24} to dimensions $\geq 3$ and in \cite{FTV23, CTV25} to regularity above the continuous threshold. Along the way, we introduce a spherical analogue of the Jones $\beta$-numbers and show that the decay of these numbers implies geometric regularity of the domain on which they are defined. We believe this result is of independent interest and partially addresses a question of Fleschler-Tolsa-Villa \cite[Question 1]{FTV23}.
item.dc:creator: Emily Casey, Max Engelstein, Tatiana Toro

item.title: Volume stability of plank covers
item.description: arXiv:2609.30409v2 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove a longstanding conjecture of Andr\'as Bezdek on the stability of plank covers of the planar disk $D$. If a sufficiently small disk $\varepsilon D$ is removed, then every finite family of planks covering the resulting annulus can be rearranged to cover the whole disk. For the proof, we establish a stronger dimension-independent stability theorem. If $K \subset {\mathbb R}^n$ is an origin-symmetric convex body for $n \geq 2$, and the uncovered region lies in $\varepsilon K$ and has volume $v$, then the excess overlap is at least $c v/\varepsilon$, where $c>0$ is an absolute constant. The proof introduces a pruning procedure and a flattening mechanism. Pruning peels away curvature through local removals whose cumulative effect is guaranteed to be substantial. Flattening trades straightness for bounded multiplicity and geometrically exposes the overlap that pays for each pruning step.
item.dc:creator: Egor Bakaev, Amir Yehudayoff

item.title: High-Index Asymptotics of Mathieu Spectral Gaps and Splittings
item.description: arXiv:2610.12751v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Consider the Mathieu operator $L=-d^2/dx^2+2a\cos(2x)$ for fixed $a\in\mathbb{C}\setminus\{0\}$. For large enough $n$, the periodic ($n$ even) or anti-periodic ($n$ odd) problem on $[0,\pi]$ has exactly two algebraically simple eigenvalues $\lambda_n^-,\lambda_n^+$ in the disc $|\lambda-n^2|<1$. We prove that, as $n\to\infty$, $\lambda_n^+-\lambda_n^-=\pm\frac{8(a/4)^n}{[(n-1)!]^2}\exp\left[-\frac{a^2(n+2)}{4(n^2-1)^2}-\frac{15a^4}{128n^7}+O(n^{-8})\right]$, where the sign depends on the labelling. For real $a$ with $\lambda_n^-<\lambda_n^+$, this difference is the length of the $n$th spectral gap. Expanding the exponential determines the relative corrections of orders $n^{-4}$ to $n^{-7}$, beyond the correction $-a^2/(4n^3)$ obtained by Anahtarci and Djakov (2012) with a relative $O(n^{-4})$ remainder. By isospectrality, the same formula holds for the potential $ce^{-2ix}+de^{2ix}$ with $a^2=cd\ne0$.
item.dc:creator: Berkay Anahtarci

item.title: Reasonable bounds for Restricted Polynomial Progressions in $\mathbb F^n_p$
item.dc:creator: Alex Burgin, Anastasios Fragkos, David Kruzel, Michael Lacey, Amelia Stokolosa

item.title: Dimension-free Markov--Bernstein-type inequality for $\mathbb R^2$-valued polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2610.13836v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove a dimension-free Markov--Bernstein-type inequality for polynomial mappings $(f_1,f_2)\colon\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^2$ of degree at most $d$. For product probability measures whose one-dimensional marginals have densities bounded by $1$, we obtain a lower bound for the integral of the Gram determinant of $\nabla f_1$ and $\nabla f_2$ in terms of the Gram determinant of the $d$-th derivative tensors $D^df_1$ and $D^df_2$, with a constant depending only on $d$. For pairs in a fixed Wiener chaos, the resulting Gaussian inequality answers a question of Nourdin, Nualart, and Poly concerning a lower bound for the expectation of the Malliavin determinant in terms of the determinant of the covariance matrix.
item.dc:creator: Egor Kosov

item.title: Hausdorff content $A_p$ weights: weighted maximal inequalities and fundamental structural properties
item.description: arXiv:2509.23839v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\mathcal H_{\infty}^\delta$ denote the Hausdorff content of dimension $\delta\in(0,n]$ defined on subsets of $\mathbb R^n$. The principal problem, considered in this paper, is to characterize the non-negative function $w$ for which the weighted $L^p$ inequality with $p\in(1,\infty)$ and the weighted weak $L^1$ inequality on Hardy-Littlewood maximal operators associated with Hausdorff content hold true. To achieve this, we introduce a class of Hausdorff content $A_p$ weights, denoted as $\mathcal A_{p,\delta}$, and then show that, for any $p\in(1,\infty)$ and $\delta\in(0,n]$, the weighted $L^p$ maximal inequality holds true if and only if $w\in\mathcal A_{p,\delta}$, and the weighted weak $L^1$ maximal inequality holds true if and only if $w\in\mathcal A_{1,\delta}$ by proposing a novel approach. As the second objective, applying this approach, the seminal structural properties of classical Muckenhoupt $A_p$ weights, such as the reverse H\"older inequality [R. R. Coifman and C. Fefferman, Studia Math. 51 (1974), 241-250], the self-improving property [B. Muckenhoupt, Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 165 (1972), 207-226], and Jones' factorization theorem [P. W. Jones, Ann. of Math. (2) 111 (1980), 511-530], are all established for $\mathcal A_{p,\delta}$. The main novelties of this paper lies in: (i) we discover $\mathcal A_{p,\delta}$ weights with rich structural properties, that increase strictly on dimension exponent and hence reduce to the classical $A_p$ class at the endpoint dimension, forming proper subsets of it for smaller dimension exponent; (ii) by proposing a novel approach, this work naturally extends the classical theory beyond measure-theoretic frameworks, while also provides novel insights even when reduced to the classical $A_p$ weight case.
item.dc:creator: Long Huang, Yangzhi Zhang, Ciqiang Zhuo

item.title: Sharp weighted norm estimates for the positive Bergman operator: the two-parameter case
item.description: arXiv:2608.01159v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We allow the exponent $\alpha$ that defines the positive Bergman operator on the upper half-plane to differ from the exponent $\gamma$ that defines the underlying weighted Lebesgue spaces. In this setting, we prove a sharp weak-type off-diagonal weighted inequality, with explicit and best-possible dependence on the B\'ekoll\'e--Bonami characteristic of the weight. We then deduce strong-type off-diagonal inequalities for the same operator. The key new tool is an off-diagonal extrapolation theorem, adapted to allow a change in the power of the distance to the boundary along the way.
item.dc:creator: Benoit F. Sehba

item.title: Directional maximal operators in the plane
item.description: arXiv:2608.23871v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This monograph investigates the Lebesgue boundedness of planar directional maximal operators $D_{\Omega}$. These are maximal averages of functions over line segments in $\mathbb R^2$ whose slopes lie in a specified set $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R$. A large body of work has identified a geometric property of $\Omega$, called finite-order lacunarity, as a key factor in ensuring that $D_{\Omega}$ is Lebesgue bounded. While several variations of this notion exist, they all centre on the distribution of gaps in $\Omega$. Building on earlier work, an article of Bateman(2009) asserted a dichotomy for such operators. Namely, $D_{\Omega}$ is bounded on $L^p$ for all $p\in (1,\infty)$ precisely when the slope set $\Omega$ is finite-order lacunary, or equivalently, when $\Omega$ does not admit Kakeya-type sets. Conversely, sublacunary direction sets $\Omega$ admit Kakeya-like phenomena, implying that $D_{\Omega}$ is unbounded on $L^p$ for all $p\in [1,\infty)$. Recent work of Hagelstein, Radillo-Murguia, and Stokolos(2024) identified a gap in the proof of this assertion and produced counterexamples for which the separation mechanism underlying that proof fails, demonstrating the need for a corrected framework. We establish the corrected characterization by introducing a new notion of admissible finite-order lacunarity that faithfully reflects the combinatorial structure of the direction set. This leads to a tree-theoretic characterization in terms of finite splitting number and provides the foundation for new geometric and probabilistic constructions establishing the equivalence between finite-order lacunarity, the absence of Kakeya-type sets, and the boundedness of directional maximal operators. The resulting framework not only resolves the gap in the earlier proof, but also identifies admissible finite-order lacunarity as the structural invariant governing these phenomena.
item.dc:creator: Edward Kroc, Juyoung Lee, Malabika Pramanik

item.title: Restriction of Fractional Derivatives of the Fourier Transform
item.description: arXiv:2410.06092v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider the differentiability of the Fourier transform of $f \in L^p(\mathbb{R}^n)$ at points on the graph of a function with non-vanishing Gaussian curvature. In particular, we show that if the values of $\widehat{f}$ along the graph possess $H^\ell$ Sobolev regularity, then this implies a certain degree of regularity of $\widehat{f}$ in the last coordinate direction as well. Two types of results are proved: One controls the $\beta$-order derivative in the last direction in terms of its $H^{-s}$ norm for suitable combinations of $(\beta, p, s, \ell)$. This extends the result in \cite{GoldStol}*{Theorem 1.12} to fractional derivatives and to some of its sharp endpoints. In particular, we recover the sharp range in the $s=0$ case where $\frac{\partial \widehat{f}}{\partial \xi_n}$ has a surface restriction in $L^2$. The second set of results is about $L^2(\mathbb{R}^n)$ bounds for difference quotients and fractional difference quotients of $\widehat{f}$, generalizing results in \cite{G2016}.
item.dc:creator: Michael Goldberg, Chun Ho Lau

item.title: Upper bound for the number of limit cycles for symmetric piecewise linear differential equations with three zones
item.description: arXiv:2507.06705v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The study of the periodic dynamics of the family of continuous observable and non-controllable three-dimensional symmetric piecewise linear systems with three zones considered here can be reduced to the study of periodic solutions of the piecewise differential equation $x'=ax+(b-a)\mathop{\rm sat}(x)+\mu\sin t$, where $\operatorname{sat}$ stands for the normalized saturation function. This paper proves that the number of limit cycles (that is, isolated periodic solutions) of the equation is uniformly bounded independently of $a,b,\mu$. Moreover, when $ab>0$, the equation has exactly one limit cycle for every $\mu>0$. When $ab<0$, it has exactly three limit cycles for sufficiently small $\mu>0$ and exactly one for sufficiently large $\mu$. When $ab<0$, using Melnikov theory for a deformation of the equation, we prove that, for each fixed $\mu>0$ away from two critical values and for sufficiently small nonzero values of the perturbation parameter, there are exactly three, five or one limit cycles, depending on $\mu$. This strengthens the conjecture that the equation has at most five limit cycles.
item.dc:creator: J. L. Bravo, V. Carmona, M. Fern\'andez, I. Ojeda

item.title: Exact versus monotone isoperimetric profiles of finitely generated groups
item.description: arXiv:2509.22260v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Gromov asked whether the exact isoperimetric profile of an infinite finitely generated group is comparable, at the same cardinality, to its greatest nondecreasing minorant. We compare finite sets with their translates and construct orders for which the first $r$ vertices have boundary bounded by a fixed multiple of that of the whole set. Such orders follow from profile summability or from rays in Schreier graphs with a uniform bound on the number using each edge. Among infinite finitely generated groups, we obtain comparison and nested exhaustions for elementary amenable and branch groups, direct products of at least two infinite groups, restricted wreath products with two nontrivial factors, and certain simple topological full groups, including amenable derived groups of interval exchanges. The exhausting $n$-point sets have boundary comparable to the monotone profile at $n$. The ray condition is quasi-isometry invariant and holds for the Sierpi\'nski-carpet group. For polycyclic groups of exponential growth, we refine Pittet's construction to obtain explicit nested sets with $|F_n|=n$ and $|\partial F_n|\asymp n/\log n$, answering his question with exact rather than comparable cardinalities. We also prove that the normalized $L^1$ profile satisfies $j(v)\le C(v/u)j(u)$ for $1\le u\le v$ on every infinite connected bounded-degree vertex-transitive graph. This yields the separation bound asked for by Gournay--Le Coz and Hume's Dirichlet--Neumann comparison at $p=1$. For groups of exponential growth, the exact-to-monotone comparison ratio is $O(\log\log n)$. We answer the first part of Correia's Question 1.3 positively by proving the required dilation regularity, and the second negatively by constructing elementary amenable examples whose inverse compositions fail this regularity for every choice of equivalent representatives.
item.dc:creator: Mayukh Mukherjee

item.title: LU-type factorizations and Darboux transformations for continuous-time birth--death processes
item.description: arXiv:2601.14074v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study LU-type factorizations of the infinitesimal generator of a possibly nonconservative birth--death process on $\mathbb{N}_0$, and characterize those for which the corresponding Darboux transformations, obtained by reversing the order of the factors, are again infinitesimal generators of birth--death processes. Two types of factorizations are considered: lower--upper (LU) and upper--lower (UL). In the LU case, the factorization is uniquely determined once the absorption rate of the Darboux-transformed process is fixed, whereas the UL factorization involves an additional free parameter. For both cases we obtain closed-form expressions for the coefficients of the factors in terms of the birth--death rates, determine the exact ranges of the parameters for which the Darboux transforms are birth--death generators, and give probabilistic interpretations of the coefficients in terms of hitting probabilities, expected passage times and occupation times. We also describe the associated spectral transformations (Christoffel and Geronimus transforms) and orthogonal polynomials, and study when the Darboux-transformed process again has a uniquely determined spectral measure: this is always the case for the UL factorization, while for the LU factorization it is characterized by the divergence of a single explicit series. The general results are illustrated with the $M/M/1$ queue, for which all the quantities involved can be computed explicitly.
item.dc:creator: Jos\'e Arcia-Manoleskos, Manuel Dom\'inguez de la Iglesia

item.title: Tangent-cone cancellation and Maz'ya's $\Phi$-inequalities on finitely cornered planar domains
item.description: arXiv:2609.12755v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $0<\alpha<2$ and $p=2/(2-\alpha)$. We study critical nonlinear convolution inequalities for kernels $K:\mathbb{R}^2\setminus\{0\}\to\mathbb{R}^m$ and functions $\Phi:\mathbb{R}^m\to\mathbb{R}$ positively homogeneous of degrees $\alpha-2$ and $p$. We assume angular Lipschitz regularity for $\Phi$ and angular $C^{0,\gamma}$ regularity for $K$, where $0<\gamma\le1$ and $\gamma=1$ if $p<2$. On bounded finitely cornered planar domains with a common Dini tangent modulus on the boundary branches, we characterize $|\int_\Omega\Phi(K*f) dx|\le C\|f\|_{L^1}^p$ for real densities $f\in L^1(\mathbb{R}^2)\cap L^s_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb{R}^2)$, $1<s\le\infty$, by signed angular cancellation on the plane, tangent half-planes, and full vertex tangent cones. An analogous criterion holds on infinite sectors for compactly supported mean-zero densities. For the Newton kernel and each nonzero angularly Lipschitz, positively two-homogeneous $\Phi:\mathbb{R}^2\to\mathbb{R}$ with vanishing half-circle moments, we construct a bounded convex $C^1$ domain $\Omega_\Phi$, independent of $\varepsilon$, and smooth tests $u_\varepsilon$ satisfying $\|\Delta u_\varepsilon\|_{L^1(\Omega_\Phi)}+\|\partial_nu_\varepsilon\|_{L^1(\partial\Omega_\Phi)}\le2$, while, despite tangent cancellation, their nonlinear integrals grow in magnitude like $\log\log(1/\varepsilon)$. On the Dini class, a constant-preserving linear extension with compact support modulo the domain mean and controlled measure-valued Laplacian yields the same necessary-and-sufficient criterion for the Newton-kernel PDE inequality, without exact corner charts. We also construct infinite-dimensional cancellation spaces containing nonquadratic functions and classify the quadratic locus in polygon moduli.
item.dc:creator: Zhouyu Long, Wenming Zou

item.title: Remarks on the Geometry of Sets in $\mathbb{Z}^d$ with Small Fourier $L^1$ Norm
item.description: arXiv:2609.26619v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study geometric inverse problems for finite sets $A\subset \mathbb{Z}^d$ whose Fourier $L^1$ norm, or Wiener norm, \begin{align*} \|A\|:=\int_{\mathbb{T}^d}\Big|\sum_{a\in A}e(a\cdot t)\Big|dt \end{align*} is subpolynomial in $|A|$. In particular, we show a variety of geometric phenomena are incompatible with small Fourier $L^1$ norm. Our principal application concerns spherical Freiman models. Suppose $\|A\|=|A|^{o(1)}$ and $D\subseteq A$ is Freiman isomorphic to a set $S$ of lattice points on a sphere; then, $|D|/|A|$ must be polynomially small in $|A|$. Moreover, if $|D|/|A|$ is not too small, almost all of $S$ lies in a small number of spherical caps, and almost all caps have rich additive structure. The proof uses a new mechanism for studying additive structure across subsets of $A$, along with decoupling results of Bourgain-Demeter.
item.dc:creator: Alex Burgin, Junzhe Mao

item.title: Exact bounds on the distribution function of isotropic log-concave distributions
item.description: arXiv:2610.10289v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For each real $b$, exact upper and lower bounds on the probability $\mathsf P(X\ge b)$ over all random variables $X$ with log-concave p.d.f.'s such that $\mathsf E X=0$ and $\mathsf E X^2=1$ are obtained, as well as the best constant factor $C$ in the inequality $\mathsf P(X\ge b)\le C e^{-b}$ for all real $b\ge0$. Exact upper and lower bounds on the corresponding exponential moments (Proposition 9.4) and explicit exponentially decreasing upper bounds on the mentioned p.d.f.'s (Propositions 9.2 and 9.3) are given as well. Some general results concerning log-concave p.d.f.'s are also obtained.
item.dc:creator: Iosif Pinelis
